speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing agitation and notice yellowing in your skin and eyes; have you noticed any dark urine or pale stools recently? To better understand the severity of this jaundice, I need to request your recent liver function tests and bilirubin levels. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Tests, Bilirubin

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bilirubin: 25 mg/dL (elevated), Liver_Function_Tests: AST 600 IU/L (elevated), ALT 650 IU/L (elevated), TP_Activity < 40% (reduced), INR 1.5 (elevated)

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Occasional use of cocaine and ecstasy. Social alcohol consumption (about 20 g on weekends).

speaker: Patient
text: The patient shows signs of psychomotor agitation and confusion. No other symptoms provided. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is unexpected, as appendicitis does not cause jaundice or abnormal liver function; could you describe how long you have felt yellow and if you are experiencing fever or right upper quadrant pain? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Patient
text: The patient shows signs of psychomotor agitation and confusion. No other symptoms provided. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That prior diagnosis seems inconsistent with your jaundice and confusion; did you recently consume large amounts of raw shellfish or have any history of liver disease? REQUEST TEST: Prothrombin_Time, Ammonia_Level. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_CT_with_Contrast.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatic Encephalopathy secondary to fulminant hepatic failure. Given the elevated ammonia, prolonged PT, and confusion, this is a medical emergency requiring immediate evaluation for liver transplantation.
